mainEntity.name: Is Nexcess the same as Liquid Web?

acceptedAnswer.text: Liquid Web is part of Nexcess. Nexcess.com is the parent brand for managed cloud, and Liquid Web sells the managed WordPress plans.

mainEntity.name: How much does Liquid Web managed WordPress cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pro WordPress starts at $19 a month for 50,000 visits. Elite starts at $29 a month. Annual billing saves 10%.
Webhostingcat measured a 202 ms time to first byte and a 433 ms Largest Contentful Paint.

mainEntity.name: Is Liquid Web good for WooCommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes for light to medium stores. Webhostingcat saw a slow checkout in its test, so test yours.

mainEntity.name: Does Liquid Web have data centers in Asia?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Sayan Samanta measured up to 1.9 seconds to first byte from India.

mainEntity.name: Does Liquid Web have a money-back guarantee?

acceptedAnswer.text: The managed WordPress page we read did not show one. Check the live terms.

mainEntity.name: Does Liquid Web include backups and staging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Daily backups are kept 14 days on Pro and 30 days on Elite, with a staging and dev site listed.

mainEntity.name: Does Liquid Web offer free migration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Liquid Web lists human-assisted migration on every plan.

mainEntity.name: Does Liquid Web have AI features?

acceptedAnswer.text: The page we read did not list any.

mainEntity.name: Is Liquid Web better than Kinsta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Liquid Web costs less at entry. Kinsta lists a money-back guarantee and published speed results in more tests.
Owners with mostly Asian visitors, beginners who want a simple host and people who need a stated money-back guarantee.
